title: Data-Dependent Probability Estimation via Sample Amplification
abstract: arXiv:2611.28399v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Can we estimate the probability of an event chosen after seeing the data, without using any fresh samples? Its empirical probability can be arbitrarily misleading, while learning the entire distribution to constant accuracy requires $\Theta(d)$ samples on a domain of size $d$. We show that $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{d})$ samples suffice for constant mean squared error, provided the rule choosing the event is known. More generally, our estimator handles arbitrary $[0,1]$-valued queries and runs in polynomial time given evaluation access to the rule. This sample complexity matches the known lower bound up to logarithmic factors and resolves the open question posed by Feldman, Kale, Raman, Talwar, and Tewari (arXiv:2610.41244).   Our estimation framework relies on a new combination of sample amplification (arXiv:1904.12053 and arXiv:2201.04315) with distribution learning via online optimization. tldr: 该论文将样本扩增与基于在线优化的分布学习相结合，提出了一种多项式时间估计器，证明在选择规则已知的条件下仅需 Õ(√d) 个样本即可对数据相关事件实现常数均方误差估计，从而解决了 Feldman 等人提出的开放问题。
en_tdlr: This paper combines sample amplification with distribution learning via online optimization to construct a polynomial-time estimator, proving that Õ(√d) samples suffice for constant mean squared error estimation of data-dependent events when the selection rule is known, thereby resolving an open question posed by Feldman et al.
